items.title: Your wearable's app, without the subscription
items.oneLiner: A warm, calm health app for a WHOOP band: recovery ring, heart rate, sleep, strain and stress on one Today screen.
youGet: A Today screen with a recovery ring and four metric cards with sparklines
Sleep, heart rate and workout screens
Your own data from Fitbit, WHOOP, Oura, Garmin or Apple Health, synced to your Mac every morning
A Hey Atu Space on your phone, or a standalone web app
items.prompt:
Build me a personal health app in the style of OpenStrap Edge (https://github.com/OpenStrap/edge).

Data: use my own wearable data. Ask me which device I wear (Fitbit, WHOOP, Oura, Garmin or Apple Watch), set up the connection on my Mac, and sync it every morning. Until it is connected, use 30 days of realistic sample data.

Screens:
1. Today: a large recovery ring (0-100%) with a one-word verdict, then four cards for heart rate, sleep, strain and stress, each with today's number and a 7-day sparkline.
2. Sleep: last night's stages as a timeline, the 14-night trend.
3. Heart rate: resting heart rate and HRV over 30 days.
4. Workouts: a list with duration, average heart rate and load.

Look: warm off-white background, white rounded cards with soft shadows, one coral accent, big tabular numbers, small labels. Numbers count up and rings draw in when a screen opens. Offer a dark version too.

Make it a Hey Atu Space I can open on my phone. Add a small line: not medical advice.

items.title: A fitness app with playful motion
items.oneLiner: Bold cards, big numbers and springy transitions between a workout list and a live session.
youGet: A workout list and a live-session screen with the same motion language

items.prompt:
Build me a workout app with playful motion, in the style of tubik's Fitness App UI Animation (https://dribbble.com/shots/9809369-Fitness-App-UI-Animation).

Data: my workouts from my watch (ask which one and connect it on my Mac), plus anything I tell you in chat ("did 3x10 squats at 60 kg"). Use sample data until it is connected.

Screens:
1. This week: a stack of bold colour cards, one per workout type, each with minutes and a progress bar to my weekly goal.
2. Session: tap a card and it expands into a full-screen session with a big timer, heart rate and the next exercise.
3. History: a calendar with a dot per workout day.

Motion: cards expand from where they were tapped, numbers count up, progress bars fill with a little overshoot. Keep every animation under 400 ms.

Make it a Hey Atu Space I can open on my phone.

items.title: A health tracker dashboard

items.prompt:
Build me a health dashboard in the style of Sigma Software Design's Health Tracker (https://dribbble.com/shots/24693286-Health-Tracker-Dashboard-UI-UX-Design).

Data: my wearable data (ask which device and connect it on my Mac), synced every morning. Use sample data until it is connected.

Layout: a greeting and today's date, then a grid of cards: heart rate (live-style line), sleep (hours and stages bar), steps (ring to my goal), calories (bar per day this week), and a weekly trend card that compares this week with last week.

Look: light, airy, generous white space, one accent colour per metric, rounded cards, large numbers. Cards fade and rise in one after another; charts draw from left to right.

Make it a Hey Atu Space I can open on my phone, and send me a short morning summary in Updates that links to it. Not medical advice.

items.oneLiner: Meals, macros and workouts in one app, with soft colours and friendly motion.

items.prompt:
Build me a diet and workout tracker in the style of Musemind's Diet & Workout Tracker (https://dribbble.com/shots/20243423-Diet-Workout-Tracker-App-Design-Nutrition-Mobile-App-UI-UX).

Data: I log meals by sending you a photo or a sentence ("two eggs and toast"); estimate calories and macros and let me correct them. Pull workouts and active calories from my watch (ask which one and connect it on my Mac). Use sample data to start.

Screens:
1. Today: a calorie ring (eaten vs goal, with burned added back), three macro bars, meals as cards with a small photo.
2. Week: calories in vs out per day, and a line for weight if I log it.
3. Workouts: this week's sessions.

Look: soft pastel cards, one strong accent, rounded type, friendly icons. Rings and bars animate when the screen opens.

Make it a Hey Atu Space I can open on my phone.

items.prompt:
I want you to create a highly professional SaaS product launch video. Go and find some SaaS, preferably just one that people know, so it's easier to identify with it. Pick that, and then make sure to get actual assets and images and all of that stuff from the internet. Turn it into these typical, very professionally edited, motion-graphics-styled product launch videos that you see people making on Twitter when they launch new SaaS products (which are showing off the features, the benefits, and all of these things).

To make one for your own product, replace the first part with: "Make it for [your product]: [link]."

items.promptBy: Hey Atu, from the creator's thread
items.prompt:
Make a 30-second launch trailer for one new feature of [your product]: [feature name].

Structure: open on the problem in one short line of big type; show the feature in a faithful rebuild of our real UI (use the screenshots I give you); end on "[feature name]. Now available in [product]" with our logo.

Build it in Remotion (React), 1920x1080, 30 fps, clean light theme, smooth easing, no stock footage. Render a take, show it to me, and keep a list of takes so I can compare versions.

items.title: A launch film like ChatGPT's
items.oneLiner: White type cards and redrawn product UI, one story from the first question to the result. The style behind OpenAI's ChatGPT launch films.
youGet: A 30-40 second launch film in this style for your own product
9:16 and 16:9 from one timeline, music and UI sounds made in code
Four stills to approve before the full render
items.prompt:
Make a {30-40} second launch film for {product}: {one sentence on what it does}.
Audience: {who it is for}. Formats: 9:16 1080x1920 and 16:9 1920x1080 from one timeline.

Follow the visual grammar of OpenAI's ChatGPT launch videos (watch
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MSiAd36bGeQ and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yyvVUEPSCu0
if you can). Copy the grammar, not their logo, words or footage.

Story
1. One story from start to end: one user, one request, one result. No topic changes.
   Use a made-up example ({e.g. "morning coffee vlog"}), never real customer data.
2. Alternate two layers: a white type card with one selling line, then a product shot.
   No voice-over; music and type tell the story. About half the time is type cards.
3. Shape: pain line (0-3 s) -> product name -> the request typed into an input box ->
   a step list the product works through -> 2-3 results, each introduced by a type card ->
   a one-line summary -> lockup with the product name.

Type cards
4. Pure white, black bold sans-serif, centred. One keyword per card in the brand colour.
5. Words appear in small groups on a 16th-note grid; when a line wraps the block moves up.
   Hold each card about 1.5 s.

Product shots
6. Redraw the UI as a clean mock, not a screen recording: large type, tidy data, only the
   parts this beat needs. Show the whole window only for results.
7. The request: the input box slides in, the camera pushes in until the text is as big
   as a title and follows the cursor as it types, then pulls back and sends.
8. Working: a "Thinking" line with a light sweep, then a step list, one row every 0.2 s,
   each with an app icon; empty circle -> spinner -> green tick; end on a large "Done."
9. Give the agent its own cursor: a black arrow with a small pill label, clicking things
   like a teammate. The user's cursor is a hand.
10. Behind window shots use a soft gradient; windows float with a soft shadow.

Motion
11. 120 BPM, one beat = 0.5 s; small moves land on 0.125 s.
12. Each shot slides in from the right by about 3.5 %, holds completely still, and slides
    out to the left by about 2.4 % just before the cut. No drifting while it holds.
13. Prefer morphs to hard cuts: a button grows into the next screen, a card shrinks into
    an input chip, the input box turns into a status pill.

Build
14. Write the film as one HTML page with a pure seek(t) function (no timers, Math.random
    or Date), render frames with Playwright and encode with FFmpeg. Keep every time in one
    timeline file that both picture and sound read.
15. Make the music and UI sounds in code (plucks on each list row, ticks on typing).
16. Show me 4 stills first (opening card, request, step list, lockup). Render the full
    film only after I approve them, then check the 9:16 version for text that wraps badly.

Do not claim things the product cannot do. Put every product fact in one copy file so I
can check it.

items.title: Raw talking head in, styled edit out
items.oneLiner: One raw clip goes in; the agent adds type, camera moves and transitions, and a video model rebuilds the scene with lips still in sync.
youGet: A vertical edit of one talking-head clip with type, camera moves and transitions
Optional restyled backgrounds from a video model
The raw and the edit side by side to compare
items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
Here is one raw talking-head clip: [file]. Edit it into a punchy 9:16 video.

1. Transcribe it and cut the pauses, false starts and filler.
2. Add kinetic captions: one to three words at a time, the key word larger.
3. Do the After Effects part in code: punch-in camera moves on key lines, title cards, transitions between sections.
4. If a video model is available, restyle the background for two or three moments, keeping my lips in sync.
5. Render a side-by-side of raw and edit so I can compare, then the final MP4.

items.title: An ad cut from 2,000 conference clips
items.oneLiner: The agent watched every clip from a conference, tagged the usable shots and cut them into ads. An honest post about what it got wrong.
youGet: A searchable library of every clip with key moments
Ads with b-roll picked from your own footage
A shortlist you approve before anything is cut
items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
My event footage is in [folder]: about [number] clips.

1. Watch every clip and log it: who is in it, what happens, the best 3-second moments, and whether it is usable (focus, framing, sound).
2. Make a searchable page of the clips with thumbnails and key moments.
3. Propose b-roll for my ad script [script]: three options per line, from usable clips only.
4. Wait for me to approve the shortlist, then cut a 30-second 9:16 ad with captions.

items.title: An edit you can finish in Premiere
items.oneLiner: The agent cuts the video, then hands back a Premiere timeline: picture on one track, sound effects grouped, music left for you.
youGet: A finished edit plus an XML timeline that opens in Premiere
One clip per track, mono audio files, every file starting at 0:00
The parts you still want to do by hand left open
items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
Edit the footage in [folder] into a [length] video: [what it is about].

When the edit is approved, export a timeline Premiere can import (FCP XML): picture on V1, voice on A1, sound effects grouped on their own tracks, an empty music track. Make every audio file mono and every file start at 0:00 so nothing drifts. Tell me how to import it.

items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
Edit my footage in [folder] into a 9:16 video about [topic], in the style of [reference video].

Then make a review page: the cut on the left, my notes on the right. I can pause at any frame and leave a note. When I say "next round", apply every open note, render V2, and show what changed for each note.

items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
Here is a [length] recording of me talking: [file], and the screen recordings I mention: [folder].

Cut it into sections. When I talk about a screen, show it full-frame with me as a small picture-in-picture in the corner. Turn the diagrams I describe into simple motion graphics. Give me a contact sheet of every shot with its timecode so I can ask for changes by number.

items.title: A Descript + Frame.io hybrid, built by an agent
items.oneLiner: A review app made for agents: word-by-word transcript, chapters, comments at a frame. Delete words to cut; the agent applies the notes.
youGet: A web app for one video: transcript, chapters, player and comments
Cut by deleting words in the transcript
Export the edit list for the agent to apply
items.promptBy: Hey Atu, based on the post
items.prompt:
Build me a review app for my video [file], like Descript crossed with Frame.io.

Left: chapters. Middle: a word-by-word transcript with speakers and timestamps; deleting words marks a cut. Right: the player and comments; I can pause and leave a note at a frame or on a selection of words. Add buttons to export the edit list (Markdown) and the comments (CSV), then apply both and render a new version.

items.title: A music video, re-imagined overnight
items.oneLiner: Given a song, a moodboard and Midjourney, the agent worked for 12 hours and returned a full music video.
youGet: A full-length video set to your track
A visual style led by your moodboard
Stills you can reuse as covers
items.prompt:
I've included an MP4 file and an original link to a video that is called "[title]". [One line about the song.]

I want you to independently do an end-to-end complete pass on making an updated version of this video. Use the exact same audio track and think and feel very deeply about what is the best way to visually represent all of the lyrics on screen. You do not need to anchor to the current style, you can do truly anything that you think might best let you visually express yourself, including abstract motion.

items.title: Three openers, three models, one prompt each
items.oneLiner: A hand-drawn story, a kinetic-type showreel and a recipe with live counters, side by side.
youGet: An opener in one of three styles: hand-drawn story, kinetic type or step-by-step
15 to 50 seconds, rendered to MP4
Your title, logo and colours
items.prompt:
Pick one:

1. A hand-drawn story: a little agent wakes up at its desk, gets feedback notes, fixes them, ends on heart eyes and a green check. 53 s.
2. A kinetic type showreel: six easing curves, a morphing star, particles, blurred type, "every frame written in code". 15 s.
3. A step-by-step White Russian recipe: ice, vodka, coffee liqueur, cream, with live counters and a checklist. 30 s.

Swap the subject for your own: your channel, your product or your recipe.
